boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented Miami University traditions, legends, ceremonies, and campus customs in Oxford.

cards.title: Rub the Turtle Heads
cards.subtitle: Tri-Delt Sundial, Quad Central
cards.notes: Find the copper turtles beneath the Tri-Delt Sundial behind Warfield and MacMillan Halls; rub a turtle head before an exam if you want to join the campus lore.
cards.short_summary: A good-luck ritual centered on the sundial’s copper turtles.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami identifies rubbing one of the Tri-Delt Sundial’s copper turtle heads before an exam as a good-luck tradition.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; consult the university campus map for current pedestrian access.

cards.entity_name: The Great Seal at the Hub
cards.title: Avoid the Great Seal
cards.subtitle: The Hub, near Upham Hall
cards.notes: Pause at the university seal embedded at the Hub, then take the long way around it to observe Miami’s long-running exam-luck superstition.
cards.short_summary: Students traditionally avoid stepping on the seal.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami describes avoiding the Great Seal at the Hub as a tradition, with lore that stepping on it brings failure on the next exam.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; consult the university campus map for current pedestrian access.

cards.title: Listen for Peabody’s Ghost
cards.subtitle: Peabody Hall, Western Campus
cards.notes: View Peabody Hall from public campus paths and treat the story as campus folklore: Miami recounts reports that Helen Peabody’s spirit watches over the hall.
cards.short_summary: A campus ghost story tied to Helen Peabody and her hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami’s traditions page documents the legend that Helen Peabody’s spirit still roams or watches over Peabody Hall.
cards.access_notes: View from public campus areas; do not enter restricted residential spaces.

cards.title: Kiss Under the Upham Arch
cards.subtitle: Upham Hall
cards.notes: Visit the archway at Upham Hall and read the posted campus legend: a kiss under the arch with a true love is said to lead to marriage.
cards.short_summary: Miami’s romantic arch legend connects a kiss with lasting love.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami calls the Upham Arch legend one of its most famous: kissing a true love there is said to lead to marriage and an unbroken bond.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; be respectful of classes and events in Upham Hall.

cards.title: Try a Toasted Roll
cards.subtitle: Pulley Diner, Armstrong Student Center
cards.notes: Order a toasted roll at Pulley Diner in Armstrong Student Center to sample the sweet roll associated with Tuffy’s Sandwich Shop and generations of Miami students.
cards.short_summary: A revived campus-food tradition from Tuffy’s Sandwich Shop.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami states that Tuffy’s specialty toasted rolls are still sold at Pulley Diner in the Armstrong Student Center.
cards.access_notes: Available for purchase at Pulley Diner; confirm current dining operations before visiting.

cards.title: Mark Charter Day at the Ball
cards.subtitle: Miami University Oxford campus
cards.notes: If its three-year cycle aligns with your visit, check university announcements for the formal Charter Day Ball commemorating Miami’s February 17, 1809 charter.
cards.short_summary: A formal, recurring celebration of Miami’s 1809 charter.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami identifies the Charter Day Ball as a tradition held once every three years to celebrate its February 17, 1809 charter.
cards.access_notes: Event timing and attendance details vary; verify the current university event announcement.

cards.title: Meet the Cradle of Coaches
cards.subtitle: Coach statues near Miami athletics facilities
cards.notes: See the bronze coach statues near Miami athletics facilities and connect them with the university’s documented Cradle of Coaches legacy in college and professional football.
cards.short_summary: A coaching legacy represented by campus bronze statues.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami documents its Cradle of Coaches tradition and notes bronze statues of iconic coaches in front of the baseball stadium.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor athletics-area display; confirm access around games and facility operations.

cards.title: Follow the Battle of the Bricks
cards.subtitle: Miami RedHawks vs. Ohio Bobcats
cards.notes: Follow Miami’s annual all-sports rivalry with Ohio University, named for the two institutions’ red-brick campuses; use official athletics schedules for individual contests.
cards.short_summary: An annual all-sports rivalry between Miami and Ohio University.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami describes the Battle of the Bricks as an annual all-sports series between the Miami RedHawks and Ohio Bobcats.
cards.access_notes: Game locations, tickets, and schedules vary; consult official Miami Athletics information.

cards.title: Spot a Miami Merger Story
cards.subtitle: Miami University alumni tradition
cards.notes: Look for Miami’s alumni features and Valentine recognition of couples who are both Miami graduates; the tradition calls these alumni pairs Miami Mergers.
cards.short_summary: Miami’s name for alumni couples who met through the university.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami defines Miami Mergers as Miami students who marry other Miami students and says it sends Valentine recognition to merger couples annually.
cards.access_notes: An alumni-recognition tradition rather than a scheduled public event.

cards.title: Learn the Mother of Fraternities Legacy
cards.subtitle: Miami University Oxford campus
cards.notes: Explore Miami’s documented Greek-letter history through its historical materials; Alpha Delta Phi established the university’s first fraternity in 1833, beginning the nickname’s story.
cards.short_summary: A campus-history tradition rooted in Miami’s early Greek-letter organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami says Alpha Delta Phi established its first fraternity in 1833 and that five social Greek-letter organizations were founded there, earning Miami the nickname “Mother of Fraternities.”
cards.access_notes: Historical context is publicly available through university resources; participation in Greek life is not required.
